title: a little help please
author: NinjaMortis
selftext: I'm working on my dread game, a horror pixel art possibly mmorpg like old school turn based final fantasy game and i was wondering what is the easiest most streamlined game engine and what other people might be using to build their games also if anyone is willing to jump in discord sometime and give me some tips and pointers or even walk me through setup I've built one game already but its just straight code no assets

comments.author: Illustrious_Art_3774
comments.body:
uhh mmorpg is going to be a far more ambitious project.

There are lots of videos that compare different game engines that you can start with or asking AI to compare them could be good to start. Godot is free so you might as well try it and see if you like it. RPG maker is built for making RPGs so that could work. It is really up to you. But 'mmorpg' is probably one to do later.

replies.author: NinjaMortis
replies.body: ha! yeah i know its huge i just cant get the idea out of my head but thanks for the advice i have tinkered with Godot so ill probably keep going down that path

comments.author: Intelligent_Art_7565
comments.body: Uhhh an MMO is a insanely huge tasks. As for an engine i mean that all depends on if it’s going to be released and charge for it. Unity and Unreal probably has mmostarter engines built. Also your wording is confusing? Whats the MMO portion of the game? I’d do alot of research use an agent to flush out your ideas first before jumping to a mmo. Start with a few small projects like a horror game, an rpg , then an online game of some sort.

replies.author: NinjaMortis
replies.body: yeah I know mmos are a huge task but I'm going to try to build the game as much as I can before try to implement any back end online stuff, if that's possible. idk if you ever played final fantasy 4 but two players could control the fights and there is an mmo that plays kind of like that called broken ranks that has some of the same systems i just don't like them but yeah ill probable work on something simple first while i world build the mmo. thanks for you help and feedback

replies.author: Intelligent_Art_7565
replies.body: Sound like you just want a coop rpg which is doable. Imma give you free game here. Take a step back and really think about the game you want to make. Who your making it for, etc. sakurai has a great game design course on youtube i always say watch to ppl. Then make a skill based off game design principles of that game director/designer. For FF4 it was takashi tokita, talk to it flush out your ideas on how this game is gonna play. Once you know what your game is have your llm mockup a prototype in html and test it see if it’s fun(<— most important part). [This is a good start on what not todo.](https://youtu.be/tPQcne7wfX8?is=rq_7IVu9uCb0FlID) User your llm to flush this out before you yolo prompt a game.

replies.author: NinjaMortis
replies.body: Oh wow thanks for the advice, I'll check it out

replies.author: ElwinLewis
replies.body: Make sure you tell your LLM to build it as an online game first because you’ll have a hard time doing it all t the end

comments.author: Silver-Chipmunk7744
comments.body: In my opinion for the most part, unless you really know what you are doing, i'd stick with three.js and browser. The AIs are often better at this, and it's much easier to reach a finished product.

replies.author: NinjaMortis
replies.body: Oh? Interesting I check it never even heard of that... Do they have a way to port it later or is that just something you can do? I know adventures quest started out as web mmo and ported it years later... Keep in mind I have barely any knowledge of what I'm talking about and I'm probably miss understanding how porting works or if that's even the correct term lol!

replies.author: Silver-Chipmunk7744
replies.body:
Well why do you want to port it?

Essentially i'd frame it this way:

Beginner: do it web based with three.js. The AI can mostly do it all, and then it's easy to publish on [itch.io](http://itch.io) or something.

Advanced: then yes doing stuff like unity makes sense, but don't expect the AI to do it all for you, and don't expect the publishing to be as simple. This is less "i vibe code everything", and more "i am the main game dev and the AI helps me a bit".

replies.author: NinjaMortis
replies.body: Id like to be able to play it on multiple platforms. Yeah I use AI for the art and game system and shit but I want to be the one to put it together I've been slowing learning Godot and I have unity too but I hardly touch it mostly just world building right now in the meantime. I'm going to look into the three.js though so that could completely change my plans lol

comments.author: Vivid_Gas_5755
comments.body: Godot's the right call for actually shipping something solo, don't let the MMO scope talk you out of starting there. Learned that the hard way. For keeping the world state consistent once you've got more than one town (a problem I ran into with a homebrew campaign tracker I hacked together), I leaned on worldos for the reactive part, Twine for straight branching dialogue when I just need text. WorldOS still gets an NPC's job title wrong every so often so double check anything load bearing. Start way smaller than the FF4 co-op idea though, that part alone will eat your year.

replies.author: NinjaMortis
replies.body: The scope doesn't scare me. I understand mmos are a huge task. Thanks for the tips and advice I'll to keep all that in mind
